theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Energy (+2.97%) and Consumer Staples (+2.02%) led the market today, while Technology (-1.66%) and Health Care (-0.83%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -0.41% versus +0.19% for defensives and +0.95% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -0.06% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -1.26%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps bucked the broader trend, with the Russell 2000 up -0.14%, outperforming large caps. The VIX rose 5.64% to 15.93, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 0.16% to $4,153.90, crude oil was little changed at $92.17, and bitcoin slipped 2.89% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
